nodes.description: (Sub)total colectomy is used when polyp burden cannot be controlled endoscopically or cancer develops; endoscopic surveillance of the remaining rectum or sigmoid continues afterwards. Data are from clinically defined SPS, not RNF43 carriers specifically.

evidence.reference_title: Low Incidence of Advanced Neoplasia in Serrated Polyposis Syndrome After (Sub)total Colectomy: Results of a 5-Year International Prospective Cohort Study.
evidence.snippet: (Sub)total colectomy mitigates much of the excess risk of CRC in patients with SPS.

evidence.reference_title: High incidence of advanced colorectal neoplasia during endoscopic surveillance in serrated polyposis syndrome.
evidence.snippet: After total colectomy, 17.9 % patients developed advanced neoplasia in the retained rectum.

nodes.description: Regular colonoscopy with removal of serrated and adenomatous polyps. The surveillance data come from clinically defined SPS cohorts, not from RNF43 carriers specifically. In those cohorts advanced neoplasia is common during surveillance while colorectal cancer incidence is low, and a randomized trial could not show that a 3-year interval is non-inferior to a 2-year interval. For RNF43 carriers, the source recommends individually tailored colonoscopy taking account of variant position and polyp history.

evidence.reference_title: High incidence of advanced colorectal neoplasia during endoscopic surveillance in serrated polyposis syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Patients with SPS have a substantial risk of developing advanced neoplasia under endoscopic surveillance, whereas CRC incidence is low.

evidence.reference_title: Endoscopic Surveillance in Serrated Polyposis Syndrome, Two or Three-Year Intervals: A Non-inferiority Randomized Trial.
evidence.snippet: In patients with serrated polyposis syndrome, extending colonoscopy surveillance to a three-year compared with a two-year interval yielded inconclusive evidence regarding non-inferiority for advanced neoplasia incidence.

evidence.reference_title: Comparison between germline and somatic loss-of-function RNF43 mutations reveals different genotype-phenotype associations and provides insights into the genetic mechanisms of colorectal tumourigenesis.
evidence.snippet: Our data do, however, suggest that once a germline RNF43 variant has been identified, a pragmatic screening approach is required, for example managing patients individually by regular colonoscopy, tailored to the position of the germline variant, polyp formation and progression over time.

nodes.description: Colorectal cancer, which can be early-onset in the reported kindreds (one proband at age 23). Population data show only a moderate overall risk increase, concentrated in N-terminal variants, and some carriers' cancers develop without contribution from the germline variant.

evidence.snippet: The proband developed microsatellite instability (MSI)– CRC age 23 years arising from a serrated polyp, in the setting of multiple (>50) large serrated polyps throughout the colon

evidence.reference_title: Comparison between germline and somatic loss-of-function RNF43 mutations reveals different genotype-phenotype associations and provides insights into the genetic mechanisms of colorectal tumourigenesis.
evidence.snippet: RNF43 is a CRC predisposition gene, but risks are moderate, the reported polyposis phenotype is often absent and molecular phenocopies can occur.

nodes.description: A heterozygous germline truncating (nonsense, frameshift) or other loss-of-function RNF43 variant is present in every cell and constitutes the first hit. RNF43 encodes a transmembrane RING-type E3 ubiquitin ligase, so the constitutional defect is a halving of a negative regulator of Wnt receptor abundance. ClinGen records heterozygous loss of function as the reported mechanism.
nodes.id: Germline Heterozygous RNF43 Loss of Function

evidence.reference_title: A deleterious RNF43 germline mutation in a severely affected serrated polyposis kindred.
evidence.snippet: We report a germline nonsense mutation within the extracellular domain of the RING finger ubiquitin ligase RNF43, segregating with a severe form of serrated polyposis within a kindred.

nodes.description: RNF43 and its homologue ZNRF3 ubiquitinate Frizzled receptors and route them to lysosomal degradation, keeping Wnt receptor levels low. Without RNF43, Frizzled receptors persist at the cell surface. This node is supported by cell-line and mouse work rather than by measurements in carriers' tissue.
nodes.id: Impaired Frizzled Ubiquitination and Wnt Receptor Turnover

evidence.reference_title: Tumour suppressor RNF43 is a stem-cell E3 ligase that induces endocytosis of Wnt receptors.
evidence.snippet: In the HEK293T human cancer cell line, expression of RNF43 blocks Wnt responses and targets surface-expressed frizzled receptors to lysosomes.

evidence.reference_title: Tumour suppressor RNF43 is a stem-cell E3 ligase that induces endocytosis of Wnt receptors.
evidence.snippet: We conclude that RNF43 and ZNRF3 reduce Wnt signals by selectively ubiquitinating frizzled receptors, thereby targeting these Wnt receptors for degradation.

nodes.description: Loss of RNF43 raises canonical Wnt signalling in intestinal stem cells and makes epithelial growth less dependent on the Wnt agonist R-spondin. Combined deletion of Rnf43 and Znrf3 in mouse intestinal epithelium produces adenomas rich in LGR5+ stem cells, and RNF43-mutant human serrated adenoma organoids and edited mouse colon organoids grow with less R-spondin1. How this Wnt gain leads specifically to serrated rather than conventional adenomatous morphology in human carriers is not established.

nodes.description: In the germline RNF43 carrier family studied at the lesion level, 62.5% of serrated polyps also carried a somatic BRAF mutation, consistent with the serrated neoplasia pathway in which BRAF (or less often KRAS) mutation is an early somatic event. BRAF activation is recorded here as a cooperating somatic event in carriers' polyps, not as part of the germline mechanism. The downstream serrated-pathway tumour biology (CIMP, MLH1 promoter methylation, BRAF V600E-mutant carcinoma) is curated in the somatic tumour entries.
nodes.id: Somatic BRAF Activation in Carrier Polyps

nodes.description: In the one germline-carrier family studied at the lesion level, all 16 serrated polyps, 5 adenomas and 1 cancer examined showed second-hit inactivation of RNF43 by loss of heterozygosity or a somatic mutation. The second hit has not been examined in most other reported kindreds (the Australian kindred report states it was not determined), so its generality is inferred from this one family and from RNF43's tumour-suppressor behaviour in sporadic tumours.
